name: IoT Analytics homepage: IoT, AI, Edge and Industry 4.0 market research
title: IoT Analytics homepage: IoT, AI, Edge and Industry 4.0 market research
answer: This is the homepage of IoT Analytics, a German market research firm covering IoT, AI, Cloud, Edge and Industry 4.0. It is a landing page rather than a full report, so it offers only report summaries and promotional claims. Its most useful concrete point is that 87% of engineering decision-makers expect AI to be embedded in their core design and engineering software, according to the firm's Design & Engineering Software Adoption Report 2026. It also notes embedded systems as a $585 billion market in 2025, with AI driving structural change.

sections.body: IoT Analytics publishes this page. It is the company's homepage, describing itself as a global provider of market insights and strategic business intelligence for IoT, AI, Cloud, Edge and Industry 4.0. The text says the firm was founded and operates out of Germany. The page is not a single research report. It is a landing page that links to or summarises several items, including the Design & Engineering Software Adoption Report 2026 and the Embedded Systems Landscape & Trends Report 2026, published August 2026. It also includes a client testimonial about independent analysis of frontier AI applications. No publication date for the homepage itself is stated in the harvested text.
sections.heading: What this source is

sections.body: The page presents IoT Analytics as a market research partner for IoT, AI, Cloud, Edge and Industry 4.0. It highlights a question about what market data on adoption, investment and enterprise deployments tells us about value creation and whether there is an AI bubble. It reports that 87% of engineering decision-makers expect AI to be embedded in their core design and engineering software, according to the Design & Engineering Software Adoption Report 2026. It says these decision-makers see value in activities such as simulation preprocessing and results interpretation. The page also states that embedded systems were a $585 billion market in 2025 and that the sector is undergoing important structural changes, according to the 87-page Embedded Systems Landscape & Trends Report 2026, published August 2026. AI is described as a major driver of those changes across hardware architecture. A client testimonial says IoT Analytics analysts provided independent analysis of frontier AI applications to support a headline for a major technology announcement. The page repeats its description as a global provider of market insights and strategic business intelligence for IoT, AI, Cloud, Edge and Industry 4.0. It does not present the underlying data, methodology or full findings for the reports it mentions.
sections.heading: What it says

sections.body: The text states that 87% of engineering decision-makers expect AI to be embedded in their core design and engineering software, attributed to IoT Analytics' Design & Engineering Software Adoption Report 2026. It states that embedded systems were a $585 billion market in 2025, attributed to IoT Analytics' 87-page Embedded Systems Landscape & Trends Report 2026, published August 2026. It also states that AI is a major driver of structural changes in embedded systems across hardware architecture. It describes IoT Analytics as founded and operating out of Germany and as a global provider of market insights and strategic business intelligence for IoT, AI, Cloud, Edge and Industry 4.0. It gives no edge deployment figures on this page.
sections.heading: Figures and claims worth noting

sections.body: A reader following AI in manufacturing would use this page mainly as a pointer to IoT Analytics' market research, not as a source of factory-floor evidence. The page connects AI to design and engineering software and to embedded systems, both relevant to industrial products and production equipment. The 87% expectation figure and the $585 billion embedded systems market give two headline data points that can frame discussions about AI adoption in engineering and hardware. The mention of edge and Industry 4.0 shows the firm's coverage area, but the page itself does not detail manufacturing deployments. For the industry page's claim that IoT Analytics measures edge deployments, this source supports only that IoT Analytics covers edge as a research area, not that it publishes specific edge deployment measurements here.
sections.heading: What it means for AI in Manufacturing

sections.body: This is a commercial homepage, not a report or independent article. It gives no methodology, sample size, definitions or full findings for the figures it cites. It does not state a publication date for the homepage. It does not provide specific edge deployment numbers, factory-floor case studies or manufacturing adoption data. The reports mentioned are behind the page, so the reader cannot verify the claims from this text alone. The testimonial is promotional and unnamed. The page is partial and dated only where it mentions report dates, including August 2026 for one report and 2026 in another title.
